summary: Reproduced all three independent-review counterexamples at candidate commit c89391648105d687cd6591fb2d501a7ab3c2c5a3, preserved the candidate's expanded accepted tool-type set, and made ResponseTool retain unmodeled fields across the typed gateway deserialize/serialize boundary.

tests.command: cargo test --test spec_test review_roundtrip -- --nocapture (candidate before correction)
tests.what_was_measured: Exact custom and namespace tool objects, plus unmodeled fields on a known tool type, were accepted but lost fields during ResponsesRequest round-trip; all 3 tests failed.
The exact custom object, nested namespace object, and independent future-field case were preserved byte-for-value at the JSON object boundary; 3 passed.
Full gateway protocol test binary passed: 95 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored, including the candidate's 12 accepted spellings and unknown-type rejection tests.
All gateway library, binary, and test targets compiled with the changed vendored protocol type and updated ResponseTool constructors.
Rust formatting check passed (with existing stable-toolchain warnings about nightly-only rustfmt options).

gpu_execution.evidence: This is deterministic CPU-only JSON deserialization and serialization behavior; no GPU execution was relevant or claimed.

remaining_limitations: GLM-5.2 weights and the reporter's four-node TP8 gfx942 deployment were unavailable, so no full model, architecture, or distributed-serving claim is made.
The regression covers the exact typed ResponsesRequest boundary used before gateway forwarding; it does not validate downstream model semantics or tool execution.
Unknown tool type spellings remain rejected, matching the preserved candidate behavior; fields on accepted tool types are now forwarded losslessly.
